**Allowed origins** are set by the `origin` callback passed to `cors()` in `worker/src/index.ts:19-35`. It is applied to every route through `app.use('*', …)`. It echoes the request origin back only if one of these is true:

- The origin is exactly `http://localhost:4200`.
- The origin ends with `.pages.dev`, which covers Cloudflare Pages at any subdomain depth.
- The origin ends with `.workers.dev`.

Any other origin, or a request with no `Origin` header, gets `null`, so no CORS headers are sent. The same `cors()` call also sets:

- `allowMethods`: GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS
- `allowHeaders`: Content-Type, Authorization
- `maxAge`: 86400

**Adding a custom domain:** edit the `if (...)` condition at `worker/src/index.ts:23-27` and add another `||` clause. Use the full origin, including scheme and no trailing slash:

```ts
origin === 'https://play.example.com' ||
```

Use `origin.endsWith('.example.com')` only if you want every subdomain allowed. A bare `endsWith` has no scheme check, and `endsWith('example.com')` without the leading dot would also match `evilexample.com`.

Don't put the domain in an array. As the comment at line 20 says, Hono matches array entries as exact strings. `worker/src/index.md:24-25` says the same, and `docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md §4` covers CORS.

After the edit, redeploy the Worker. I didn't check whether the frontend's API base URL in `frontend/` also needs changing for the new domain.
